objective: Do Gate 5's critical results (the D_-topology disentangling finding, and D_full's advantage over CNN/ViT on H2/H3-C) replicate across independently-retrained backbone seeds, not just re-seeded probe heads on a single frozen checkpoint?

design.training_stability_recheck: D_full, CNN-baseline, ViT-baseline, and D_-topology were each independently retrained at seed=1 and seed=2 (seed=0 already existed from Phases 3/4/5) using the identical recipe/budget as their original runs -- no hyperparameter changes.
design.backbone_seed_probe: jobs/probe_multiseed_job.py re-runs the exact H3-C topology probe and H2 data-efficiency AULC methodology (same target, same single-Linear probe architecture, same probe_seed=0) against all 12 checkpoints (4 architectures x 3 backbone seeds), extracting model.encoder.encode_hidden(x) (or the architecture's own equivalent) mean-pooled -- identical extraction to gate_5_h3c_topology.json/gate_5_h2_data_efficiency.json/probe_ablations_job.py.
design.scope_note: Only D_full, CNN, ViT, and D_-topology were re-seeded -- D_-topology because it is the single most decisive Gate-5 finding (the whole disentangling claim); D_classical/D_-complex/D_-graph/D_-prob remain single-seed (seed=0 only), a real, explicitly acknowledged scope limit, not an oversight.

seed_ci_vs_baseline_point_estimate.method: t-distribution 95% CI, n=3, df=2, t_crit=4.303, sample std (ddof=1) -- n too small for a normal approximation to be defensible; ddof=1 used deliberately since ddof=0 (population std) understates uncertainty at this sample size and was caught and corrected during this gate's own drafting, not shipped uncorrected
seed_ci_vs_baseline_point_estimate.interpretation: D_full's advantage over CNN/ViT is statistically robust across backbone seeds -- its CI excludes both baselines' point estimates on both metrics, and does not even overlap CNN's own CI. D_-topology's mean is statistically indistinguishable from CNN/ViT on both metrics (its CI comfortably contains both) -- the Gate-5 collapse-to-baseline finding is NOT a single-seed artifact.

data_gaps: D_classical/D_-complex/D_-graph/D_-prob remain single-seed (seed=0) -- not re-seeded in this gate, real scope limit.

Only H2/H3-C were re-seeded at the backbone level (the two positive findings the paper's headline claim rests on). H1/H3-A/H3-B/H4/H5 were not re-run at additional backbone seeds -- their Gate-5 verdicts (nulls and one FAIL) were not the ones requiring reproducibility confirmation to support or refute the headline claim.
Section 21 (distribution shift across genuinely different datasets) remains unaddressed, unchanged from Gate 5.
decision_rule: PASS iff the Gate 5 verdict (D_full's H2/H3-C advantage is real; D_-topology collapses that advantage to baseline level) is stable across seeds -- operationalized as: D_full's 95% CI (n=3 backbone seeds) excludes both CNN's and ViT's point estimates on both metrics, AND D_-topology's 95% CI contains both CNN's and ViT's point estimates on both metrics. Both conditions met.
interpretation: Both training-stability (all 12 seed x architecture runs PASS, 0 NaN/Inf) and the actual scientific reproducibility check (backbone-seed CI analysis above) confirm Gate 5's central finding is not a training-seed fluke. D_full's margin over CNN/ViT is tight and highly consistent (std 0.006-0.008 on both metrics, CI not even overlapping CNN's own CI) -- about as clean a reproducible effect as this vault has produced. D_-topology is reproducibly collapsed to baseline level, but also reproducibly noisier across seeds (std 0.029-0.037, roughly 4-6x D_full's own seed variance) -- ablating the topology signal doesn't just remove the mean advantage, it destabilizes the representation's seed-to-seed consistency too, a real secondary finding worth carrying into the paper alongside the primary one.
